name: ual_parse
description: Read a Microsoft 365 unified audit log export offline (portal or PowerShell CSV with an AuditData column, JSON with that wrapper, native audit events as an array, JSON Lines or a value envelope, a Graph audit log record) and open the payload: `audit_data` is the whole AuditData as written (Name/Value, NewValue/OldValue and duplicate parameter names kept), beside the lifted fields (operation, user, address, workload, record type, result, record id, MailAccessType, OperationCount, items listed) and each record's file, record and line. `status` and `status_basis` say whether every row was read; a row that is not an audit record (counted in rows_not_audit_records), a row that could not be processed for any other reason (counted and listed, and the read goes on), a file of a directory skipped for its name (named in skipped, and the read is partial), a payload that is not JSON (kept with its outer columns), a file that is not an audit export, a CSV line past the field limit, an archive (.zip, tar: named, not read), a next-page marker, an export whose own ResultCount says more records matched than it holds, and files not reached before the time limit are counted separately, located and listed. Time: AuditData's CreationTime, else the outer column; no zone is not UTC unless assume_utc says so (a native CreationTime with no zone included, and a row left undated says so in time_zone), a day/month/year string needs a date_order or unambiguous rows that prove one (reported), and a declared date_order that a row contradicts leaves that row undecoded, named; raw and decoded times are kept; since/until exclude rows whose time could not be read and count them (status is then partial). record_type matches the payload's RecordType and the outer column, by number or by name as the export wrote them (the export's own pairing is shown in record_types_all_rows; no number-to-name table is built in), and a filter value that matched no row is reported. Summary tables describe the matched records; operations_all_rows and record_types_all_rows are every row, withheld the same way. `user` is a regex (at most 200 characters) matched against the user as printed, never against a withheld original; a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, and every test of any pattern is timed: one test that takes more than a quarter of a second fails the call, named. An argument the tool does not have is refused. `notable` names an operation, not its meaning: MailItemsAccessed is not a statement that content was read. NOT measured: whether the audit configuration or licence captured every operation (aggregation and duplicate suppression can apply: check the schema the export carries), or who a record's user is. SENSITIVE: parameters and properties can hold secrets; a field named or shaped like a credential is withheld and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT; run as a job with secret_output: true. An out_file is never replaced by a smaller result; a read that ended early publishes it as <name>.partial<ext> and names it partial_records, never complete_records, and SIGTERM leaves no temporary file. A record larger than max_record_bytes in an array or an envelope is skipped by scanning to its end without holding it (the scan is under the clock and holds one chunk), counted and located as rejected (its offset, line and length), and the records after it are read; the file is partial and the reason says so. Zero bytes after the last gzip member are padding (GNU gzip ignores them): they are counted as trailing_zero_bytes in the file's census row, are not damage and do not keep a read from complete; zeros followed by anything else are not padding. Every problem of a gzip file (a member failing its CRC-32 or its length, a stream cut short, bytes that are not another member) is kept, in order: the first 25 are listed in the file's problems and the rest are counted. Each record carries parser ual_parse/7; the label moves when what a record says changes. The export's own pagination is checked: rows of one ResultCount are one search and must hold the ResultIndex values 1 to that count, each once, in any order; a repeated index, a missing one, a value outside 1 to the count, rows with an index beside rows without one, and a count this tool does not check the indices of (more than 64 distinct counts in a file, or more indices than its bitmaps hold, 2^28 in all) are each a named pagination problem (pagination_markers, with the first 25 repeated, missing and out-of-range values), and the read is partial; a ResultCount above the rows the file holds is named as before. Withholding (the shared block of every pack that withholds, with a 1 MiB gate here and 64 KiB elsewhere), from version 12: every slot has one treatment. Identifiers are printed as they are and judged by nothing (event, request, correlation, object and record ids, access key ids, ARNs, account ids, hashes a record names); every other string, file name, path, JSON pointer, table key and message goes through the credential rules only (never the rules for identifier-shaped runs, which would withhold the identifiers); a field that is named like a secret goes through the name layer whatever its value is. New in this version: a Name/Value pair whose Value is a number or an array, the NewValue after an OldValue, a Value over 4,096 characters, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, curl -u user:pass and a bcrypt hash are withheld (they were printed). Known gaps: an array Value nested in another or over 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, a secret with neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: An export (CSV, JSON, JSON Lines; the format is read from the content) or a directory of them

operations.description: Keep only these operations (compared without case, as printed; a value that matched nothing is reported as given)

user.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the user as printed; a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, and every test of any pattern is timed (a quarter of a second)

since.description: ISO 8601 lower bound (a bound with no zone is UTC); a row whose time could not be read is excluded and counted

until.description: ISO 8601 upper bound (a bound with no zone is UTC)

record_type.description: Keep only these record types: the number or the name, matched against the payload's RecordType and the outer column as the export wrote them, without case or white space and a number without leading zeros (no built-in table pairs a number with a name; a value that matched nothing is reported as given)

notable_only.description: Only the operations this tool lists for a second look

assume_utc.description: Read a time that carries no zone as UTC. Say so only on the export's own documentation or collection record; each record's time_status says it was assumed

date_order.description: mdy or dmy, for day/month/year strings whose two leading fields are both 12 or less

format.description: auto (default: from the content), csv or json

delimiter.description: CSV delimiter, one character (default a comma)

max_field_bytes.description: Largest CSV field read (default 16 MiB, at most 1 GiB); a larger one stops the file, named, with what was read kept. A CSV line is held to max_record_bytes

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for every matching record, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Never replaces a file already there: that one is kept and this one is named beside it

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); past it the whole list is in a file the answer names (under $OUT/tool-output in a job, work/<agent>/tool-output otherwise)

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB; a CSV line too); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut (in an array or an envelope it is skipped by scanning to its end without holding it, and the records after it are read)

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 420, at most 480, so the answer is written well inside the 600 seconds a call has); the limit is checked inside a record too, and a record it cuts is counted and listed; what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. The manifest declares secret output for it: a job with write_values runs as secret output whether or not the agent set the flag, and its values file is sealed sensitive. Honoured only in a job whose SECRET_OUTPUT is 1; outside a job, or in a job that is not secret output, it is refused as JSON and nothing is written
